_note: Retrieval gold for Stage 10/11. For each incident: the failure class whose runbook and post-mortem are the right documents (primary, relevance 2), classes that are also useful (secondary, relevance 1), a 'paraphrase' query (an engineer's description of the symptoms) and a harder 'symptom' query that deliberately avoids the vocabulary used in runbooks. Queries describe what is observable, never the root cause. Uses the frozen dev/test split in eval/splits.json; tune only on dev.

INC-001.paraphrase: checkout-api CPU is pinned near its limit and latency keeps climbing while traffic looks normal
INC-001.symptom: the checkout service is running flat out and requests are piling up behind it even though nobody is sending more traffic

INC-002.paraphrase: checkout-api pods keep getting killed for running out of memory and garbage collection takes longer every time
INC-002.symptom: checkout containers keep dying and coming back, and they seem a little fatter every time before they go

INC-003.paraphrase: checkout-api and payment-service are both failing with timeouts and open circuit breakers and it is unclear which one started it
INC-003.symptom: checkout and payments are both unhappy, everything calls something that is stuck, and alarms started going off all over the place

INC-004.paraphrase: error rate on checkout-api jumped with the same exception repeating right after the latest version went out
INC-004.symptom: checkout started throwing the same crash on every order a few minutes after we shipped the new build

INC-005.paraphrase: checkout-api requests time out waiting for database connections to orders-db and the pool looks full
INC-005.symptom: checkout requests are stuck waiting in line to talk to the orders database although the database itself is not melting

INC-006.paraphrase: notifications-service cannot write anything and the logs keep complaining about storage
INC-006.symptom: the notifications box has nowhere left to put anything and its housekeeping jobs are failing

INC-007.paraphrase: checkout-api and inventory-service keep losing connections to each other with resets and retransmits although both are healthy
INC-007.symptom: two of our services cannot hold a conversation with each other, calls get cut off halfway, but each one is fine on its own

INC-008.paraphrase: payment-service calls to the outside payment provider are failing with server errors and timeouts
INC-008.symptom: everything on our side is fine yet payments fail because the company we pay through is not answering properly

INC-009.paraphrase: checkout-api cannot reach an internal service because the hostname lookup fails
INC-009.symptom: checkout insists that an internal service does not exist, though it was there yesterday

INC-010.paraphrase: clients refuse to connect to checkout-api and secure handshakes fail since early this morning
INC-010.symptom: since this morning browsers and partners refuse our secure connection although the servers are up

INC-011.paraphrase: notifications are arriving hours late, the queue keeps growing and the consumers keep rebalancing
INC-011.symptom: messages do get through but hours late, the line keeps getting longer and the workers keep reshuffling who does what

INC-012.paraphrase: inventory-service pods keep restarting and failing their readiness checks
INC-012.symptom: the inventory containers start, die, start again and never reach the serving state

INC-013.paraphrase: checkout-api is overloaded with high CPU and a growing request queue but the number of replicas never goes up
INC-013.symptom: load is way up and the service is drowning but nothing extra has been started to help

INC-014.paraphrase: checkout-api gets unauthorized responses from auth-service since this morning's credential change
INC-014.symptom: ever since the password change checkout is turned away by the auth service though nothing else changed

INC-015.paraphrase: checkout-api shows a retry storm in production that never happens in staging, as if one setting is different
INC-015.symptom: production does something odd that our test environment never did, as if the two were set up slightly differently

INC-016.paraphrase: one node is taking most of the traffic and users get bad gateway responses from it
INC-016.symptom: one server is doing nearly all the work and visitors keep getting bounced at the front door

INC-017.paraphrase: orders-service has latency spikes that line up with long JVM pauses
INC-017.symptom: the orders service freezes for a moment every so often and then carries on as if nothing happened

INC-018.paraphrase: cart-service is slow and database CPU is high even though traffic is moderate, with a flood of tiny queries per request
INC-018.symptom: the cart page is slow and the database works hard for a modest number of visitors, doing the same small lookup again and again

INC-019.paraphrase: search-service CPU alert fired but dashboards and logs look completely normal
INC-019.symptom: an alarm woke us for the search service but when we looked everything seemed perfectly healthy

INC-020.paraphrase: notifications-service keeps running out of memory with the heap near its limit and containers being killed
INC-020.symptom: notifications workers keep running out of room and being killed, same story as a while ago

INC-021.paraphrase: inventory-service latency and CPU alert while pods are being drained and rescheduled during a change window
INC-021.symptom: inventory looks shaky right now but the platform team said they are moving machines around today

INC-022.paraphrase: search-indexer CPU and memory are high with slow query warnings during the nightly job
INC-022.symptom: the search indexer is working very hard at the same time as every night and complaining a bit, but customers are fine

INC-023.paraphrase: ledger-service throughput graph collapsed exactly when the metrics exporter restarted but ledger entries are still being committed
INC-023.symptom: the ledger graph fell off a cliff yet the ledger keeps saving entries, and the monitoring agent was just touched

INC-024.paraphrase: catalog-api traffic quadrupled and the rate limiter kicked in for one client during a scheduled performance run
INC-024.symptom: traffic on the catalog api shot up and one visitor is being throttled, apparently the performance people are at it

INC-025.paraphrase: reporting-service heap usage keeps creeping upward with warnings about approaching the limit but nothing has crashed yet
INC-025.symptom: reporting is slowly eating more and more memory day by day, warnings but no outage so far

INC-026.paraphrase: orders-api times out on database connections after an approved maintenance finished and configuration was refreshed
INC-026.symptom: the planned work finished and was declared a success, but orders are now timing out on the database

INC-027.paraphrase: some auth-proxy pods get credential rejected errors from billing-api after the scheduled secret rotation while others work fine
INC-027.symptom: after the scheduled credential swap a few of the proxy replicas are refused by billing while their siblings are fine

INC-028.paraphrase: email-worker stopped consuming and queue depth is growing right after the nightly batch was enqueued, consumer heartbeat missed
INC-028.symptom: the email sender went silent right after the nightly bulk job dumped its messages and the line keeps growing
